broader_review_uses.connection_to_review: Contextualizes the role of advanced imaging in solid tumor management beyond traditional anatomical MRI.
broader_review_uses.material: Discussion of WHO 2021 CNS tumor classification requiring better prediction of tumor nature than weighted MRI provides. Mentions potential for AI/Radiomics analysis of mp-qMRI data to predict contrast enhancement, radio-necrosis vs recurrence, and tumor subtypes.
broader_review_uses.purpose: Background on the evolution of imaging biomarkers in neuro-oncology/solid tumors.

broader_review_uses.connection_to_review: Illustrates challenges in translating advanced MRI techniques to clinical routine.
broader_review_uses.material: Limitations section notes the need for inter-vendor harmonization and demonstration of clear benefit to patient outcomes to increase clinical acceptance.
broader_review_uses.purpose: Example of barriers to adoption of novel diagnostic tools in oncology.

facet_contributions.boundaries: Specific to brain tumors and 3T MRI. Does not provide data on efficacy modulation by microbiome or ICI response mechanisms.
facet_contributions.contribution: Provides a validated, fast (8 min) mp-qMRI protocol for brain tumors. Details the acquisition parameters (mGRE, EPI) and processing steps for generating T1, T2*, H2O, and susceptibility maps. Shows that these quantitative maps can be acquired rapidly enough to be added to routine clinical workflows.
facet_contributions.possible_uses: Can be used to discuss the feasibility and standardization of advanced imaging biomarkers in solid tumor trials. Illustrates how quantitative metrics (beyond size/volume) are obtained.

facet_contributions.boundaries: Focuses on technical quantification accuracy rather than biological mechanisms of drug action or immune response.
facet_contributions.contribution: Demonstrates the necessity of individual-specific correction for water relaxation times in MRS quantification. Shows that using literature values leads to significant errors (~15-35%) in both healthy and tumor tissues. Proposes a method to synthesize water references using qMRI, improving accuracy.
facet_contributions.possible_uses: Highlights the importance of precise biomarker quantification in assessing tumor metabolism. Can support arguments about the need for rigorous standardization in imaging biomarkers used to monitor therapy response.

planning_summary: This material provides technical methodology for advanced neuroimaging biomarkers (qMRI and MRS) in solid tumors (brain tumors). It offers specific protocols for acquiring quantitative tissue properties (T1, H2O, susceptibility) and precise metabolite quantification. While it does not address gut microbiome or immune checkpoint inhibitors directly, it serves as a critical background for understanding how advanced imaging biomarkers are standardized and quantified in oncology, which may be relevant for discussions on non-invasive monitoring of treatment response or tumor microenvironment characterization in solid tumors.
scope_interpretation_cautions: This paper focuses exclusively on brain tumors (a type of solid tumor) and does not cover other solid tumor types. Findings on imaging biomarkers are specific to the central nervous system context.
The study validates technical accuracy and reproducibility of imaging protocols, not clinical efficacy or therapeutic outcomes related to immunotherapy or microbiome interactions.

The 'proposed method' for MRS quantification relies on specific assumptions (e.g., T2 estimation from T2*) that may not generalize to all scanner vendors or pulse sequences without further validation.
title: Development of a fast multi-parametric quantitative MRI protocol for brain tumor imaging and its application in absolute quantification of cerebral metabolites using MR-Spectroscopy
